oneliner.t: Three-term Republican U.S. representative from Enterprise (AL-2 2021–2025, AL-1 since 2025), former state legislator and waste-hauling business owner, who won the June 16, 2026 GOP runoff with Trump's endorsement and faces Democrat Everett Wess for Alabama's open Senate seat.

born.t: September 26, 1966, Coffee County, Alabama (birth date from Wikipedia; age 59 in May 2026 per Alabama Reflector is consistent)

upbringing.t: Moore (legal name Felix Barry Moore) grew up on a family farm in Coffee County in Alabama's Wiregrass region. He joined the Alabama Army National Guard (records reported by the Alabama Reflector date Guard service 1988–1991, followed by Individual Ready Reserve status to 1997). He earned an associate degree at Enterprise State Community College and a B.S. in agricultural science from Auburn University in 1992, where he met his wife, Heather. After a first job in the animal-pharmaceutical industry, he returned to Enterprise and started an industrial waste-hauling company with his wife. The couple have four children and attend Hillcrest Baptist Church in Enterprise.

career.role: Alabama Army National Guard (about 2.5 years), then Army Reserve (about 5.5 years); honorably discharged; basic-training active duty Mar–May 1989; never deployed
career.org: Alabama Army National Guard / U.S. Army Reserve

career.role: Co-founder/owner, industrial waste hauling and general contracting company
career.org: Hopper-Moore Inc. (also described as Barry Moore Industries / BMI)

career.role: State Representative, District 91; chaired Military and Veterans Affairs Committee

platform.t: Pledges to stand with President Trump, 'have his back and defend the MAGA agenda in the Senate'; endorsed by Trump (Jan. 2026) and VP Vance.
Secure the border, deport people in the U.S. illegally, make English the official language, prosecute officials who obstruct federal immigration enforcement.
Cut taxes (including on tips, overtime and Social Security), cut regulation and the size of government; says he will lower inflation by reducing the national debt.
Campaigned on ending stock trading by members of Congress.
Full funding for law enforcement; prosecute violent criminals and antifa-linked groups, which his site blames for the 2020 riots.
Opposes federal gun confiscation; touts an NRA 'A' rating.
Restrict women's sports to biological women and cut federal funds to those who don't; anti-abortion; opposes 'the Democrat trans agenda'.

Sponsored House bills targeting Sharia law: a March 2026 bill to bar Sharia-based discrimination by public accommodations and a May 2026 'CRUSADE Act' requiring EB-4 religious-worker visa applicants to disavow Sharia law.
Has voted for the crypto industry's top legislative priorities, holds an 'A' from Stand With Crypto, and is backed by crypto-funded super PACs.
Fund the VA, protect the GI Bill, support military families.

promises.t: Back President Trump's agenda in the Senate.
Secure the border and deport people in the country illegally.
End stock trading by members of Congress.
Lower inflation by reducing the national debt.
Cut taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security.

claims.claim: Born and raised in Coffee County; grew up on a farm there.

record.t: Born in Coffee County on Sept. 26, 1966; spent much of his youth on the family farm.

claims.claim: Was the first elected official in Alabama (2016) — and, elsewhere on the same page, the first in the nation (August 2015, Mobile rally) — to endorse Donald Trump.

record.t: No independent tally of the first elected official to endorse Trump was found. The page itself gives two versions (first in Alabama in 2016; first in the nation in Aug. 2015).

claims.claim: Owns a waste removal and demolition company.

record.t: He co-founded and co-owns the industrial waste-hauling firm now called Hopper-Moore Inc. with his wife; his 2025 House disclosure lists the stake (95%) in his spouse's name.

claims.claim: Rated the most conservative member in Alabama by CPAC while in Congress.

record.t: CPAC's 2022 ratings gave Moore 91%, tied with Sen. Tuberville for highest in Alabama's delegation (one year's rating).

claims.claim: Rated Alabama's most effective legislator by the 'Center for Legislative Excellence'.

record.t: No organization by that name or rating was found. The Center for Effective Lawmaking's published Alabama scores cover 2019–2022, after he left the legislature, and do not mention him.

claims.claim: At Auburn he enlisted in the Alabama National Guard, joined Auburn's ROTC program and earned a degree in agricultural science.

record.t: B.S. agricultural science, Auburn, 1992; enlisted in the Guard while at Auburn; was on Auburn's ROTC Army Ranger Challenge Team.

claims.claim: Met his wife Heather at Auburn; married 33 years.

record.t: Met Heather Hopper at Auburn; married in 1992.

claims.claim: After college he and Heather founded BMI, Inc. with one garbage truck; it has grown for 20+ years.

record.t: Founded the waste-hauling company Barry Moore Industries in 1998 (Wikipedia), now Hopper-Moore Inc., operating 'more than two decades' (Encyclopedia of Alabama). The one-truck detail was not independently documented.

claims.claim: In 2010 he defeated a six-term Democratic incumbent to win his Alabama House seat.

record.t: He defeated Democrat Terry Spicer in 2010 (9,754–5,383). Spicer served District 91 from 1998 to 2010 — three four-year terms, not six.

claims.claim: In the Alabama Legislature he fought for military families' in-state tuition and sponsored bills to shield service members from unfair family-court procedures and to honor military spouses' out-of-state licenses.

record.t: He chaired the Alabama House Military and Veterans Affairs Committee, but Alabama Legislature bill records for these specific bills were not retrieved.

claims.claim: Serves on the House Judiciary Committee.

record.t: Serves on the House Agriculture and Judiciary committees.

claims.claim: Has passed laws to ensure veterans receive their earned benefits.

record.t: No specific enacted law was named, and congress.gov sponsorship records could not be retrieved.

claims.claim: Has repeatedly voted to cut taxes.

record.t: One such vote is documented: Aye on final passage of H.R. 1 (July 3, 2025). A full tax-vote history was not compiled.

claims.claim: Won the Congressional Management Foundation's Workplace Environment award in 2023.

record.t: CMF gave his office a 2023 Democracy Award in the 'Life in Congress' Workplace Environment category.

claims.claim: He and Heather have four children, and he still lives in Coffee County.
claims.short: Four children; lives in Coffee County

record.t: Four children; lives in Enterprise, which spans Coffee and Dale counties.

claims.claim: The 2020 riots were the direct result of radical left antifa organizations.

said.where: campaign site Issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) — Law and Order (claim 3)

record.t: A broad causal characterization, not a single checkable fact.

claims.claim: Under Joe Biden, federal law enforcement was aimed at Trump supporters and conservatives.

said.where: campaign site Issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) — Law and Order (claim 4)

record.t: A contested characterization of prosecutorial intent, not a single checkable fact.

claims.claim: In Trump's first term, working-class wages grew faster than elite wages for the first time in fifty years.

said.where: campaign site Issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) — The Economy (claim 6)

record.t: Atlanta Fed data showed the lowest-paid quarter of workers getting larger percentage raises than the top quarter since 2015, a trend that began before his term and that CBS tied partly to state minimum-wage increases. No source was found for the 'first time in fifty years' part.

claims.claim: The One Big Beautiful Bill gives working families and small business owners a real tax cut.

said.where: campaign site Issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) — The Economy (claim 7)

record.t: The law cut taxes, including new deductions for tips and overtime. But CBO's analysis of the House-passed version found household resources would generally fall for the lowest-income households (largely due to Medicaid and SNAP cuts) and rise for middle and top households.

claims.claim: Under Biden the southern border 'invasion' strained police, hospitals and schools; under Trump the borders are now secure.

said.where: campaign site Issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) — Border Security and Immigration (claim 10)

record.t: 'Invasion' and 'secure' are characterizations rather than checkable measurements.

claims.claim: 'A+ rated by the NRA.'

said.where: TV ad 'Shoot You Straight' (six-figure buy, Montgomery/Birmingham/Huntsville; most-covered Moore Senate ad)

record.t: NRA ratings were not retrieved. His own Issues page says 'A rating from NRA Action', which does not match the ad's 'A+'.

claims.claim: 'President Trump endorsed me.'

said.where: TV ad 'Shoot You Straight'; also TV ad 'D.C. Garbage' (2026-04-02)

record.t: Trump endorsed Moore for the Senate in January 2026.

claims.claim: 'I've run a business, met a payroll' and 'hauled garbage.'

said.where: TV ad 'D.C. Garbage' (2026 Senate version; second most-covered Moore Senate ad)

record.t: He founded and co-owns an industrial waste-hauling company.

said.t: Opposed the Fiscal Responsibility Act, saying it would 'saddle Americans with $4 trillion in new debt'; also opposed raising the debt ceiling in 2021. Campaigns in 2026 on reducing the national debt.

did.t: Voted Aye on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), which raised the debt limit by $5 trillion and which CBO estimated would add trillions to deficits over a decade (figures reported range from $2.8T to $3.4T depending on the estimate). The bill also contained spending cuts he supported.

said.t: 'Any threat to Israel is a threat to the United States and our freedoms.'

did.t: Voted Yea on H.R. 8034, the $26 billion Israel Security Supplemental.

saydo.topic: Tax cuts on tips and overtime

said.t: Says he fought for tax cuts on tips and overtime.

did.t: Voted Aye on H.R. 1, which enacted those deductions.

promises_prev.promise: Support a constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms and senators to two (signed U.S. Term Limits pledge to cosponsor and vote for it; 'I support term limits for Congress').

evidence.t: He served three House terms (2021–2027) and is now seeking a Senate seat instead of a fourth House term, which fits the pledge's three-term House limit. Whether he cosponsored the term-limits amendment in each Congress could not be verified (congress.gov was not reachable).

complicating.t: The pledge commits him to cosponsor and vote for the amendment; no term-limits amendment has passed Congress. Cosponsorship status needs a human check on congress.gov.

promises_prev.promise: Keep supporting President Trump's agenda (2020 campaign).

evidence.t: He objected to Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes in January 2021 and voted for Trump's 2025 tax-and-spending law (H.R. 1); Trump endorsed him for Senate in January 2026.

complicating.t: A broad loyalty promise rather than a specific policy; listed because it was the central theme of his 2020 campaign.

entries.t: Voted against the Fiscal Responsibility Act (debt-limit deal), objecting to '$4 trillion in new debt'.
Voted for H.R. 1, which included a $5 trillion debt-limit increase.
Voted Yea on Israel aid (H.R. 8034) and Nay on Ukraine aid (H.R. 8035) the same day.

note.t: 2025 annual report (filed Apr. 29, 2026): biggest asset is the spouse's 95% stake in Hopper-Moore, Inc. (listed $1M–$5M), plus two commercial properties, a home in Enterprise, a River Bank & Trust brokerage account and a small 'Coinage' account (Mother Jones reports a 2024 disclosure showed $1,001–$15,000 in bitcoin). checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener (courtlistener.com/?q="Barry Moore" Alabama) and Justia searches were tried directly and were blocked for this research tool (no approval granted), so courts are 'news': APR/APR.org/Ballotpedia/Wikipedia reporting on the 2014 perjury case (acquitted; Alabama Supreme Court rejected his pretrial challenge). Alacourt is paywalled and was not searched. Ethics: searched the Office of Congressional Conduct (formerly OCE) lists directly — 117th Congress (all 6 pages), 118th Congress, and the running investigations list through 2026-03-02. Moore is not named. House Ethics Committee pages could not be fetched directly; a site search and two committee press releases turned up nothing on him. A 2021 STOCK Act complaint against a 'Rep. Moore' concerned Blake Moore (R-Utah).
checks.foreign: 2025 House annual financial disclosure (no foreign assets, income or positions). FARA: reached efile.fara.gov, but its name search is an interactive form the tool cannot submit, and the bulk CSV downloads are zipped binaries it cannot read, so no FARA name search was completed ('no'). News searches found no foreign-government or foreign-business ties.
checks.claims: Mechanical v2.1 sample: (a) every checkable claim on barrymooreforalabama.com/about (15 rated); (b) the first 10 statements on barrymooreforalabama.com/issues — #1 (record boast), #2, #5, #8 and #9 are position statements or too vague to check, and #3, #4 and #10 are rated 'opinion'; #6 and #7 are rated; (c) ad spend is unknown, so the two most-covered 2026 Moore Senate ads were used: 'Shoot You Straight' (2026-04-22, six-figure buy; ADN and Yellowhammer) and 'D.C. Garbage' (2026-04-02; Yellowhammer). Earlier claims outside this sample were dropped: Guard length, veteran status, staff-sergeant title, self term-limiting, 'most conservative' AP quote, Heritage 98%/NRA A (Issues items 13–14, beyond the first 10) and tips/overtime.
checks.democracy: Clerk of the House roll calls 10 and 11 (Jan. 6–7, 2021); APR reporting on his January 2021 tweets; Wikipedia.

legal.t: Arrested in April 2014 on two felony perjury counts and two counts of making false statements, tied to a Lee County grand jury investigation of House Speaker Mike Hubbard. He had been recorded pressuring primary opponent Josh Pipkin to drop out. A jury found him not guilty on all counts on Oct. 30, 2014. Before trial, the Alabama Supreme Court rejected his challenge to the grand jury and the special prosecutors' appointment (Sept. 2014).

recordx.note: 2025 annual House disclosure filed 2026-04-29, before the May 15 deadline. missed_pct is missing because GovTrack (member ID 456800) returned errors on three tries. fec is missing because the FEC committee filings/RFAI tab loads by script and showed no rows, and the FEC API and legal-search pages are robots-blocked.

research_notes: MONEY: FEC candidate totals (S6AL00476, thru 2026-06-30) combine three authorized committees: C00720375 (his former House committee, now 'Barry Moore for U.S. Senate', which holds nearly all the money), C00954974 (new principal committee registered 2026-07-01; no reports yet) and C00903518 (nominee fund). The Q3 2026 report (due Oct. 15) and the pre-general report were not yet in FEC data on 2026-10-08. Debts of $360,928.39 include a $50,000 candidate loan; the rest is not itemized here. 'Other committee contributions' of $881,597.83 (the pac_all field) could not be split into business vs. ideological PACs because OpenSecrets is blocked and the FEC API is unreachable, so pac_biz/pac_ideo/earmark are omitted. 'other' = $234,460.16 in transfers from authorized committees plus $5,661.25 in other receipts. Quarterly figures: the 2025 total is from Ballotpedia (receipts thru Dec. 31, 2025) and Q1-26 is $902,931 from an 1819 News headline; later quarters were not available. No OpenSecrets industry or top-donor data was retrieved, and in-state % was not computed. OUTSIDE MONEY: the Defend American Jobs figure is 'more than $5M in February plus $1.7M in May, nearly $7M' (Mother Jones), entered as 6,700,000, a lower bound. Crypto-press headlines say crypto PACs had about $12M at stake in the runoff, but this was not confirmed from FEC independent-expenditure data (FEC IE pages blocked by robots.txt). Amounts for Club for Growth's Alabama Freedom Fund (pro-Moore), Fellowship PAC (pro-Moore), American Conservative Fund ('stolen valor' ad against Moore; WVTM reportedly pulled it) and Hudson- or Marshall-aligned PACs were not found. No general-election outside spending was found. ISRAEL: AIPAC's own endorsement list and AIPAC PAC earmarks to Moore were not checked (Track AIPAC gives no AIPAC-specific dollar figure). No UDP spending was found (Track AIPAC IE = $0). NOT FOUND: GovTrack missed-vote % for the 119th Congress (govtrack.us returned 403; search snippets gave no figure); Center for Effective Lawmaking score; counts of bills sponsored or enacted (congress.gov blocked); cosponsorship of term-limits amendments; independent verification of the Heritage Action 98% and NRA 'A' ratings; GENIUS/CLARITY crypto roll calls. Campaign website URL not confirmed (Ballotpedia's contact email uses barrymooreforalabama.com; the 2020-era barrymooreforcongress.com domain has lapsed). The photo was left out because no official portrait URL was found. DEBATES: 'declined' = Jan. 5 and Jan. 8, 2026 primary forums he did not attend (Wikipedia).
